newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on bargain hunting.

text.p: Thai stocks, which moved in a narrow range and negative zone for most of the day, closed up 1.43 percent after investors bought some key stocks at bargain prices and on a technical rebound, brokers said.
The SET index, which fell in the past six consecutive days, ended 12.57 points up at 889.46 on 2.7 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 1.35 points to 67.49.
"The index rose today because of a technical rebound after it fell quite heavily in the past few days. Late bargain hunting was another factor behind the rise," said a broker at Asia Credit.
"The gains in the SET index were in line with increases in several regional markets today," said the broker at Asia Credit who asked not to be identified.
Brokers said the rise in the SET index came after investors bought some finance, building, energy and bank stocks.

Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, topped the active list, falling four baht to 198. National Finance and Securities rose 1.50 to 55 while TelecomAsia advanced 1.50 to 54.50 and television operator BEC World was unchanged at 250.
The market will be closed on Tuesday for the Constitution Day holiday. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
